key_insight: For parameter-noise SGD, the simplest design works best: isotropic noise with a single perturbed forward pass captures most of the gains of more complex perturbation schemes.
engineering_relevance: Practitioners can improve training and generalization with a low-overhead noise-injection strategy that preserves batched computation and avoids elaborate noise parameterizations.
method: Use a distributional identity for linear layers to apply per-example perturbations without breaking mini-batch efficiency.
Compare isotropic noise against several diagonal Gaussian parameterizations.
Test whether multiple perturbed samples per update meaningfully improve performance over a single noisy forward pass.
evidence_signal: On CIFAR100, the authors systematically evaluated multiple noise levels and found that simple isotropic noise with one perturbed pass per update matched most of the benefit of more complex approaches.
watch_item: Per-example noise injection depends on the linear-layer identity and careful implementation to preserve batched computation and avoid unintended efficiency or correctness issues.
paper_title: Simplicity Suffices for Parameter Noise Injection in Stochastic Gradient Descent
